records.summary: The National Bank of Iraq's 2024 annual report says Ayman Omran Abdullah Abu Dahim was Acting Head of the Financial and Banking Studies Unit at the Banking Institute, affiliated with the Saudi Central Bank, before joining Capital Bank Group in Jordan as Chief Financial Officer in 2011; he has been a board member and Chief Executive Officer of the National Bank of Iraq since 15 April 2018. The same report's shareholder table, for 2024, lists Jordan Capital Bank Company with 61.85 per cent of NBI, Cairo Amman Bank with 9.9 per cent, Al Bawadi Al Khadra with 9.59 per cent and Arcadia LLC with 5 per cent, each a company rather than a state body, and the report adds that the bank enjoys no governmental protection or privileges. The ownership table is from 2024 and the move to Capital Bank was in 2011, thirteen years earlier; the report does not say who held the shares in 2011, and his biography adds that he sat on the Capital Bank board representing Jordan's General Organization for Social Security, a state pension body, so the state pension fund held some Capital Bank shares at some point. No source read here says Capital Bank or NBI was ever state-owned.
records.source_title: National Bank of Iraq, Annual Report 2024, Board of Directors and Executive Management (pp. 163-165)

records.summary: BOA Madagascar's own 2014 annual report records, in its calendar of the year, that in November 2014 Alain Herve Rasolofondraibe, Chairman of the Board of Directors of BOA in Madagascar, was appointed Governor of the Central Bank of Madagascar; the incoming chairman's letter in the same report pays tribute to him and wishes him well in his new responsibilities as Governor. The same report gives the bank's share register as at 24 April 2015: 41.26 per cent AFH-Ocean Indien (the BOA group holding), 10.40 per cent the International Finance Corporation, 9.45 per cent FMO of the Netherlands, 4.40 per cent Proparco, 24.83 per cent Malagasy private shareholders, 9.37 per cent the Malagasy State and 0.29 per cent other shareholders. The share table is dated 24 April 2015, about five months after the November 2014 appointment, and the report does not give an earlier table; on that table the Malagasy State holds a minority 9.37 per cent and the bank is majority held by the BOA group, development finance institutions and private Malagasy shareholders. Nothing in the report says the bank was state-owned at any point.

On ownership, the bank's own presentation page calls AFG Bank Comores a subsidiary of the financial holding company of Atlantic Group, founded by the Ivorian businessman Kone Dossongui, and its history page says the panafrican Atlantic Financial Group bought BNP Paribas' shares in October 2020. records.people: Damche Tenzin (Chief General Counsel, Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan, from 1 June 2016)
records.summary: Damche Tenzin's own curriculum vitae, published by Bhutan's Financial Institutions Training Institute, says he has been Chief General Counsel of the Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan, the central bank, since 1 June 2016, and that before that he was Chief Legal Advisor and Company Secretary at the Bank of Bhutan from 1 September 2008 to 6 December 2014, then Chief General Counsel at the National Pension and Provident Fund from 1 January 2015 to 30 May 2016. Both of those outside employers are state bodies rather than private firms: the National Pension and Provident Fund is Bhutan's state pension fund, and Bank of Bhutan is a subsidiary of Druk Holding and Investments, the government's commercial holding company. This record is filed as a public move for that reason and should not be counted on the revolving-door row. I did not obtain a readable ownership page for Bank of Bhutan: the DHI portfolio page at dhi.bt served a 404, so the state ownership of Bank of Bhutan is stated here from the CV's own framing of the posts and not from an ownership table.

records.summary: The Central Bank of Sudan's own page for Abdall Hassan Ahmed lists his posts in order: General Manager of Faisal Sudanese Islamic Bank from 1985 to 1990, Minister of Finance and National Economy from 1993 to 1996, then Governor and Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Sudan from 1996 to 1998; earlier he was General Manager of the Islamic Investment Company 1983-1985 and Deputy Manager of the Islamic Insurance Company 1980-1983. Faisal Islamic Bank (Sudan) is privately owned: the bank's own shareholders page gives 11,352 shareholders, with individual shareholders holding 63 per cent and companies 37 per cent, and 78 per cent of the shares held by non-Sudanese holders, and its own establishment page says eighty-six Sudanese and Saudi founders and citizens of other Islamic countries met in May 1977, subscribed half the capital, and registered the bank as a public limited company on 18 August 1977. The shareholders page carries recent figures (its tables run to 2021) while the post was held from 1985 to 1990, so the table and the post are from different periods; the establishment page covers the founding as private, and no source read here says the bank was state-owned at any point in between.
records.source_title: Central Bank of Sudan, Governors of CBOS: Abdall Hassan Ahmed

held.note: Second Sudan find, career sentence in hand, ownership sentence missing. The Central Bank of Sudan's own page for Awad Abdel Magied Aburiesh (https://cbos.gov.sd/en/node/618) says he joined Barclays Bank in London as local director at the level of general manager's assistant in 1960, became the first General Manager of Bank of Khartoum (ex Barclays Bank) after nationalisation in June 1970, was Deputy Governor of the Bank of Sudan in 1969 and Governor and Chairman from July 1971 to October 1972, and set up his own private business, Awad Abdel Magied and Partners Ltd, in 1973. The Barclays post is the private one, and the same page says the Sudan business was nationalised in 1970, so the private window is the 1960s. I could not open a Barclays ownership page: home.barclays/investor-relations/shareholder-information/share-price-and-calculator/ and /shareholders-hub/ both served 404 and the shareholder-information index page carried no listing statement. What would close it: the major-shareholders note in Barclays PLC's own annual report at https://home.barclays/investor-relations/reports-and-events/annual-reports/ , or Barclays' 1960s-era company history page.

Career sentence half in hand, private employer not named. State House Seychelles (https://statehouse.gov.sc/news/1861/new-central-bank-board-member) says Bertrand Rassool was Director of Research at the Central Bank of Seychelles from 1980 to 1987 and that his private sector experience includes key positions in both Seychelles and Mauritius, including in the financial sector, but it names no employer. Two nation.sc pieces on him were read and give no career history. What would close it: a Central Bank of Seychelles annual report board-profile section, e.g. the governance chapter of the CBS annual reports at https://www.cbs.sc/Publications/annualreports.html . Also noted: Jean-Paul Barbier, CBS 2007-2017 and Director of its Financial Services Supervision Division, was delegated the role of Manager of BMI Offshore Bank Ltd from November 2014 to June 2015 while still at the CBS (https://nation.sc/articles/20653/cbs-thanks-outgoing-member-of-its-board-and-welcomes-new-board-director-). That reads as a supervisory assignment by the central bank rather than private employment, so it is held, not filed.

The BOL record is filed, but on the central bank's own wording that the period was spent in private enterprise, not on a share register. What would close it: a shareholder table for Banco de Cochabamba S.A. or Compania Boliviana de Seguros S.A. ASFI's Historia de la Supervision tomo I remains the route named last round; ASFI's MEMORIA_1998.pdf (https://www.asfi.gob.bo/images/ASFI/DOCS/MEMORIAS/MEMORIA_1998.pdf) was read this round and lists Banco de Cochabamba S.A. only under entities in liquidation, with no ownership classification, so that document does not close it. Note also that curl gets 404 from asfi.gob.bo but WebFetch reads it.
